title: CHECK Constraint
description: Learn how to use the CHECK constraint to enforce domain integrity by limiting values in a column.

data.text: The CHECK constraint allows you to specify the values in a column that must satisfy a Boolean expression. It enforces domain integrity by limiting the range of values that can be inserted or updated in a column.

data.title: CHECK Constraint as Column Constraint
data.content: Limits unit_price to positive values only.

data.text: You can also assign a constraint a separate name using the CONSTRAINT keyword:

data.title: Named CHECK Constraint
data.content: Creates a table with a named CHECK constraint for better error messages.

data.text: Explicit names help classify error messages and allow you to refer to the constraints when you want to modify them.
The following insert statement violates the CHECK constraint because the unit price is 0:

data.title: INSERT Violating CHECK Constraint
data.content: Fails because unit_price is not greater than zero.
data.code:
INSERT INTO test.products(product_name, unit_price)
VALUES ('Awesome Free Bike', 0);

data.text: SQL Server returns an error: The INSERT statement conflicted with the CHECK constraint "positive_price".

data.title: INSERT Satisfying CHECK Constraint
data.content: Succeeds because unit_price is greater than zero.
data.code:
INSERT INTO test.products(product_name, unit_price)
VALUES ('Awesome Bike', 599);

data.text: CHECK Constraint Referring to Multiple Columns
A CHECK constraint can refer to multiple columns. For example, ensuring that a discounted price is always lower than the regular price:

data.title: Multi-Column CHECK Constraint
data.content: Ensures discounted_price is always less than unit_price.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE test.products(
    product_id INT IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    unit_price DEC(10,2) CHECK(unit_price > 0),
    discounted_price DEC(10,2) CHECK(discounted_price > 0),
    CHECK(discounted_price < unit_price)
);

data.text: Adding CHECK Constraints to an Existing Table

data.title: Add CHECK Constraint with ALTER TABLE
data.content: Adds a CHECK constraint to an existing table.
data.code:
ALTER TABLE test.products
ADD CONSTRAINT positive_price CHECK(unit_price > 0);

data.title: Drop CHECK Constraint
data.code:
ALTER TABLE test.products
DROP CONSTRAINT positive_price;

data.title: CHECK Constraint Key Points
points: CHECK constraints enforce domain integrity by limiting column values.
The Boolean expression must evaluate to TRUE for the row to be inserted or updated.
You can define CHECK constraints as column constraints or table constraints.
Named constraints make error messages clearer and are easier to manage.
NULL values bypass CHECK constraints since NULL evaluates to UNKNOWN.
